reviews.review: Gaming's equivalent to a movie you find while channel surfing on a Saturday. You never bother to learn the title, but you stick with it until the end for reasons unknown. You will not remember anything about this happening within an hour of the conclusion (other than the fact that the enemies shouted "SPACE MARINE" 30 times in each of the 1000 uninteresting combat encounters that the game constantly throws your way). Just change the channel.

If killing hundreds of thousands of orks in bloody, visceral, meat chunk flying, all encompassing, all out war is your idea of fun, then this is the game for you. It is "spectacle fighter" and shooter in the Warhammer 40,000 universe, what more needs to be said. It is not a crazy innovative title but it looks prett decent and is fun as hell.

Not a bad game but it is definitely not a masterpiece too. In this game  your main objective is kill everybody. It have good atmosphere not bad graphics for few years old game. And see THQ amblem in beggining is priceless.

If you're a fan of any WH40K-related material, this is a must.

"Space Marine" is a hybrid hack 'n' slash / 3rd person shooter where you assume the role of Captain Titus of the Ultramarines, whose 3-man team is dispatched to forge world Graia to aid in the defense against an Ork invasion. Once on ground, Titus uncovers a deeper and more sinister plot that could - of course - threaten the security of not only Graia, but the Imperium of Man.

While the story is fairly standard, everything else excels. Visually the game is stunning in bringing to life a forge world. "Bleak and uninspiring environments" are the adjectives tossed around by critics, but a forge world in WH40K lore is exactly that: a giant factory spanning the whole world whose sole purpose is to produce industrial goods (mostly war-equipment). That said, the game had me staring in awe at some of the grandiose Adeptus Mechanicum architecture, monuments to the Omnissiah, Titan war-machines, giant guns, etc. It's a world at war, and you - as the player - constantly feel it as shells streak down from the sky, ships crash-land, enemies run and shoot on and off-screen.

As the Emperor's finest, you are the Space Marine - the most perfect warrior in the galaxy. You start with a simple bolt pistol and a short-sword, but during the course of the game you will acquire plenty of bolt and energy-based long-range weapons as well as melee weapons. These range from the core Space Marine weaponry such as: chainswords and bolters, to power axes, power hammers, grenade launchers, lascannons, snipers, plasma guns, grenades, etc. Each weapon handles differently, and each has its use. Indeed,  no weapon is useless if you know how to use it.

I found the gameplay most enjoyable on HARD difficulty. While the game can be truly punishing - since you face overwhelming odds at all times - you will be forced to use tricks & tactics in every battle. So you'll have to pick your weapons carefully for each situation since you can't carry them all at once. While seemingly very simplistic at first, the game forced me to constantly adapt my approach for each enemy group and kept me on edge at all times.

Last but not least, the soundtrack by Cris Velasco and Sascha Dikiciyan is an amazing orchestral arrangement of might and thunder, in the vein of the best "God of War" musical pieces.

I haven't touched the multiplayer, so no comment on that. The single-player campaign will last you about 13-15 hours on HARD; and if you liked it, you'd probably want to go through it again. So that's about 15-30 hours of single-player experience. and for me it was worth the money.
